title: I decided to try AI to quickly create a browser game client and I'm not looking back
author: DungeonDelveQuest
selftext:
I spent a lot of time creating the API for the game, but in terms of testing it, AI was the perfect tool for me getting a basic client application up and running quickly and provided me with a quick feedback loop for changes. The AI requires a lot of input and trial and error to get things right, but it also allowed me to test various aspect before deciding on what direction I wanted to go. I'm not saying the AI art that was produced is perfect (far from it), but it's good enough for the phase I'm in. 

There is a real stigma about AI in games, which to some degree is understandable, but to quickly go from idea to a mock up made with AI is invaluable, and I'm convinced the game industry introduce it more and more, to the point where gamers would be hard to find a game where AI was not involved.

The game I'm working on, Delve ([http://dungeondelve.quest](http://dungeondelve.quest/)), is a browser based dungeon crawler game that is more about strategic thinking and resource planning than combat animations (there aren't any). The dungeon is semi-shared and there is a multiplayer aspect to it.

I've made an early version that is free to play and looking for feedback from players that think this sounds interesting. I'd also like feedback on what direction I could go in with the client, and how AI could assist me with that.
